text: Driverless cars should be legalized, but only under a licensing regime that treats the software vendor as the driver. The usual fear is a robot that cannot handle a wet intersection. The better fear is an uninsured stack of neural nets with no one to sue. Cities that already run automated metros show that machines can move people when the operator remains legally on the hook. Vendors would then compete on safety records instead of marketing slogans. Opponents argue that edge cases will always remain. That is true of human drivers too, and we still issue licenses. The difference is that a fleet can be recalled overnight; a million tired commuters cannot. Legalization without liability would be reckless. Legalization with vendor liability is how aviation already works, and it is how the roads should work next.

text: Phones should be banned during lessons, not during the whole school day. When a notification lights up, attention splits, and the student who was following a proof is suddenly in a group chat.
